name: Pest control

pf.license.need: Yes, where the state's form says so (nearly every state): a pest control license or registration for the company, and an applicator license for each person who applies pesticides.
pf.license.categories: By category: general pest, termites and other wood pests, fumigation, lawn and shrubs. Each person is offered only for the categories their license covers.
pf.license.ask: The company's license or registration number at sign-up. Each applicator's number and categories in their invite reply.
pf.license.who_holds: Both: the business, and each applicator. Where a state lets a technician work under a certified applicator, the state's form says how.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: Pest control and lawn spraying go live on the company's license. Each applicator is offered once Sam says yes.
pf.license.insurance_bond: Where the state's form asks for insurance or a bond, it's asked at sign-up. It is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.shop: A bug ID at the counter needs no license. Where a state licenses pesticide sales, the shop's form asks for that license.
pf.license.not_this_work: Wildlife removal (raccoons, bats, squirrels) is its own kind of work, with its own permits where a state requires them.

words: a sting with swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, or feeling faint
bait, pesticide or spray swallowed by a person
someone sick after a spray, or a pesticide spill
a wasp nest or a swarm by a door, or inside the home
what_happens: A sting with a reaction: call 911 now, and use an epinephrine pen if they have one. No booking until everyone is safe.
Bait or pesticide swallowed: call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 with the label, or 911 if they aren't breathing, can't wake up or have a seizure. No booking in that chat.
A pet that ate bait: call a vet or a pet poison line, with the label. Rosie points to the business's line; the booking can go on.
A nest by a door: keep children and pets inside, use another door, and don't spray or hit the nest. The booking goes on, soonest first.
Honey bees: a beekeeper is suggested first.
Questions about whether a product is safe for pets, children or a pregnancy are answered only by the licensed applicator or Sam. Rosie never answers them.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: Yes, after the safety steps, for a nest by a door or a pet that ate bait. No, for a sting with a reaction or anything a person swallowed, until everyone is safe.
pf.safety.re_entry: How long people and pets stay off treated areas comes from the product label, from the applicator at DONE or Sam's settings. Rosie never makes up a time.

pf.first_steps.inspection_first: Termites: a free inspection with a written report, then a contract. Bed bugs: an $89 inspection, credited to the treatment. Mice: priced at the visit. Ants, roaches, spiders and wasps book straight in.
pf.first_steps.notice: The written pesticide notice, where the state's rules require it: the pests, the products and their active ingredients, a caution line and who to call. It goes before the first treatment, by email and a secure link; to the owner too when a renter booked; and again when a product changes.
pf.first_steps.neighbors: A lawn or shrub spray, where the state's rules require it: a notice to registered neighbors, or a sign posted, a set number of hours ahead. Sam gives it himself; Rosie never texts neighbors. Not given in time: only the inside part goes ahead.
pf.first_steps.plan: A plan starts after the first service. Cancelling the first service also ends the plan that starts after it.
pf.first_steps.bed_bugs: A bed bug treatment needs its prep list done first (about 3 days): clothes and bedding bagged and dried hot, the floor around the beds cleared. Its 2 visits are booked together.
prep_for_reminder: Put food, dishes and pet bowls away
Clear the kitchen cabinets where the pests are seen
Cover fish tanks and turn off their air pumps
Keep pets where you said, away from treated rooms
Don't spray store-bought bug spray before the visit
pf.first_steps.shop: Bring the bug sealed in a bag or jar, frozen if it's alive. Never carry in a live wasp or bee: a photo works.

pf.visit.check_in: Someone home: the code at the door, entered by the applicator. Inside work needs an adult (18 or older) home to let the applicator in. Outside-only work: no code; DONE with a photo.
pf.visit.order: The applicator inspects first, reads the private note, then treats inside first and outside last.
pf.visit.health_note: A health note changes the products, like bait gel instead of a spray, at the same price.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: Extra work (a wasp nest found) is priced before it's done, with the customer's yes. Mouse work is priced at the visit. A right to cancel where the state's rules give one for work sold at the home.
pf.visit.other_pests_found: Signs of termites or bed bugs: today's visit goes on, and an inspection is offered as its own booking, only if the customer wants it.
pf.visit.proof_done: The service report before DONE: products and their registration numbers, active ingredients, amounts, areas treated, the applicator and license, the label's re-entry time, and the weather for outside work.
pf.visit.re_entry: With DONE, the applicator texts the label's re-entry time, and Rosie passes it on word for word.
pf.visit.weather: The product label's rain and wind limits: an outside spray moves to another day at no cost; the inside part goes ahead.
pf.visit.shop: At the counter: the code at check-in; the tech names the bug under a magnifier while the customer waits. Nothing is applied at the shop.

pf.money.start: A card saved at booking, charged at DONE (the example business's choice). Rosie's starting answer for visits at the home, the $89 trip charge held, is also offered. Some customers get the bill by text instead.
pf.money.paid_ahead: Nothing is paid in full ahead. Routine visits, plans and one-time jobs like a wasp nest are charged at DONE or billed after. Only contract work (rodent-proofing, termites, fumigation) takes a deposit, after the contract is signed.
pf.money.deposits: None for routine visits. Rodent-proofing, termite treatment and fumigation: a deposit only after the written contract is signed (the example: 25%). Deposit cap: from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel or nobody home for inside work: the $89 trip charge (the example), only if Sam confirms each time; no answer, no fee.
pf.money.plans: Each plan visit is charged at its own DONE. A free re-service between visits is $0. Rosfield's $2 counts once a month for a plan.
pf.money.tips: No tip line unless Sam turns it on.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes pest control, from the state form.
pf.money.shop: Lee Pest Supply (the example shop): nothing taken when booking, and no card saved, so no fee; paid at the counter, the shop's own way. A bug ID at home takes nothing either: Rosie texts the bill after.

never_in_texts: Health reasons to avoid a spray, like asthma, allergies or a pregnancy
pf.messages.notice: The pesticide notice goes by email and a secure link, never as a long text.
pf.messages.languages: English and Spanish. The notice and the prep list in the customer's language where the business has it.
pf.messages.minors: Nobody under 18 books. A teen at home isn't the adult who lets the applicator in.
pf.messages.after_stop: After STOP, plan reminders and notices go by email.

pf.staff.licenses: Each applicator holds a state applicator license in each category they work in. Where the state allows it, a technician works under a certified applicator, as its form says.
skills: General pest, wasps and mice: Kevin and Marco
Rodent-proofing, termites and lawn spraying: Kevin only
Bug IDs at the shop: Nina and Mei; heat treatments: Nina only
pf.staff.stand_in: Only someone licensed in the same category. A stand-in the customer didn't book is offered first; no reply by the deadline, the stand-in keeps the time.
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs any price over $500 made for one customer. Pat may too; Sam's answer wins.
pf.staff.safety_questions: Only a licensed applicator or Sam answers a question about a product's safety.

pf.rules.label: Every product is used only as its label says, including re-entry times and weather limits (federal law). Rosie's texts give the label's time from the applicator, never one of its own.
pf.rules.notice: A written pesticide notice before the first treatment, to the people who live there and the owner, where the state's rules require it; sent again when a product changes.
pf.rules.service_report: A service report after each treatment, kept with the job, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.termite_contract: Termite work: a written contract the property's owner signs before any work or money, saying what the guarantee covers, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.neighbors: A notice to registered neighbors, or signs posted, before a lawn or shrub spray, where the state's rules require it.
plans: The plan's terms show before any card: how often, the price a visit, when it's charged, that it runs until ended, and how to end it.
The plan gets its own yes, apart from the booking, and the terms are texted back.
A price change is told 30 days ahead, or more where the state's rules ask.
Any reminder the state's rules require while a plan runs.
pf.rules.add_on_at_home: A right to cancel where the state's rules give one for work sold at the home.
pf.rules.show_license: The company's license number on the times, the confirmation and the receipt, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, or longer where the state's rules ask for treatment records.

matter_most: Pests come back between plan visits: a free re-service.
A sting, or a product swallowed: the safety words first.
Rain over the label's limit: the outside part moves at no cost; the inside goes ahead.
A neighbor notice not given in time: only the inside part goes ahead.
A renter books: the owner gets the notice too.
Signs of termites found at a visit: a free inspection offered, as its own booking.
Pets, fish and children: kept off treated areas until the label's re-entry time.
A health note: bait instead of a spray, same price.
Skip, pause or end a plan, and a plan's price change.
Several open bookings, like a re-service and the next plan visit: which one is asked first.
Nobody home for inside work: the trip charge only if Sam confirms.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
Pilot: cleaner (from). Pest control runs like a set service: a visit at the home on a plan that repeats every 3 months, a card saved and charged when the work is done, and visits with nobody home for outside work. The cleaner's shape fits better than the plumber's (repairs priced at the visit). What the cleaner lacks is added: licensed applicators, the written pesticide notice, the service report and the label's re-entry time, inspections first for termites and bed bugs, and signs of termites found at a visit.,Flow B is the usual side: Lee Pest Control (pest control, plus lawn care as its second kind of work, both licensed by category). Flow A is the less usual side: Lee Pest Supply, Sam's own shop company, where a customer brings a bug to the counter and a licensed counter tech names it (a $35 bug ID), or books it at home ($75, the both-places service).,Names: Jordan and Casey become applicators Kevin and Marco (he fits the master's pronouns). Riley and Avery become counter techs Nina and Mei. The master's partner Jamie is Taylor (Jamie is a cleaner pilot name). Addresses: 410 Commerce Dr (the company), 26 Cedar Ave (the shop), 19 Maple Ct (Alex's home). The old flowchart's Sierra Shield, Teresa, Kevin and Danielle gave the story; Kevin stays as the applicator.,Prices are the example business's own, never facts about pest prices. The master's numbers are kept so sums still add up: $179 first service (the old flowchart's $189), $89 trip charge (late cancel, nobody home, a hold, and the price-at-the-visit promise; the old $50 fee becomes it), $150 wasp nest removal, $640 rodent-proofing from photos, $245 mouse control priced at the visit (seal entry points $165, traps $80), $500 OK limit. New: $249 one time, $129 a plan visit, $99 outside spray. Shop: $35 bug ID, $40 termite sample check, $20 quick photo ID, $25 tick ID, $55 DIY plan, $140 belongings heat treatment, $90 furniture heat treatment from photos, $75 bug ID at home.,The master's 'service call' is 'trip charge' here, and its 'visit fee' too (the cleaner pilot uses 'visit fee', so the leftover-word check flags it).,Money, flow B: main list|card|card (a card saved, charged at DONE), as the old flowchart. Also used: list|hold|card (Rosie's starting answer for visits at the home, the $89 held), list|none|bill (some customers get the bill by text), visit|card|card (mouse control priced at the visit). Nothing is ever paid in full ahead: the wasp nest removal follows the starting answer (review, Oct 22: list|full|none was listed only because the master's sign-up set the nest that way; dropped, and S1-13/S1-16/S1-17 reworded). No deposit on routine visits; rodent-proofing, termite treatment and fumigation take a deposit only after their contract is signed (B8-28's 25%, B8-62, B8-63). Rodent-proofing is quoted at a visit (a mouse visit or an inspection), never from the customer's photos, so there is no photos path (S1-12/S1-13 say so). S11-56's what-if moves the outside spray from the $89 hold to a card saved, both used here.,Money, flow A: list|none|counter only. Every shop service takes nothing ahead, saves no card (so no fee) and is paid at the counter (S1-42, S1-45, S1-47 say so); the shop holds no money (A7-02's day-before hold is off). The bug ID at home ($75) takes nothing either: Rosie texts the bill after, on the other flow's list|none|bill path; the shop's Stripe is for that bill (S1-49, S1-51). S11-54 in flow A has no plan notice: the shop sells no plans. S11-04, S11-06 and S11-86 say no card was saved; S11-72 is Lee Pest Control's cancelled extra work (the shop sells no memberships, and A10-05's contract branch is off).,The plan is an event, not a money choice: the price question asks plan or once (B4-05: $179 first service on the plan, $249 once), B4-44 shows the plan's terms, B5-21 takes its own yes (a no shows $249 before any card), and the own split B6-x01 texts the terms back. Free re-service between visits is the master's warranty branch (B10-08).,Own steps, flow B: B6-x01/B6-x02 (the plan's terms texted back, from the cleaner pilot), B8-x01 (the label's re-entry time passed on word for word after DONE), and the branch 'Signs of termites' on B8-22 with B8-x02 (a free termite inspection offered as its own booking). The written pesticide notice is the master's own notice steps (B4-28, B7-30) with pest words; the service report is the master's visit record (B8-55, B8-56).,The neighbor notice before a lawn or shrub spray is the master's 'The business gets it first' (B4-42), Sam's to-do; Rosie never texts neighbors. A moved visit re-checks it (B7-06). Rain moves only the outside part (B7-35 more line).,A renter: B4-78 always asks own or rent (its 'No: nobody asks' branch is off); the owner gets the pesticide notice through a link the renter forwards (B4-35, B4-36 more lines).,Safety: the plug-in's danger words are a sting with trouble breathing and a product swallowed (B3-19's words, with Poison Control's national number). A nest by a door is Rosa's safety-steps call (B3-18). A pet that ate bait goes to the business's own line (B3-21). Product safety questions go only to the licensed applicator or Sam (B7-16).,Off as never used, flow B: sent now (B4-81, B6-03, B7-55, B8-58), set starts, stays, seats and no-person times (B4-83), warranty plans paying, stock held, crews and equipment, host visit days, damage holds, delivery and setup, outside checks, items to the shop, several-day jobs, permits, reports ready later, rentals, parts billed after, stage bills, insurance.
